They collide when the positions agree: $2\cos t=2\cos t$ always, and $2\sin t=3-4\sin t\Rightarrow\sin t=\frac12$, first at $t=\frac\pi6$.

Velocities: $\vec v_1=\langle2\cos t,-2\sin t\rangle=\langle\sqrt3,-1\rangle$ and $\vec v_2=\langle-4\cos t,-2\sin t\rangle=\langle-2\sqrt3,-1\rangle$.
\[\cos\theta=\frac{\vec v_1\cdot\vec v_2}{|\vec v_1||\vec v_2|}=\frac{-6+1}{2\sqrt{13}}=\boxed{-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{13}}}\approx-0.693.\]

$D=vt$ with $v=100$ km/h and $t=50$ s $=\frac{50}{3600}$ h, so $D\approx1.389$ km. Then $dD=t\,dv+v\,dt$:
\[|dD|\le\frac{50}{3600}(2)+100\cdot\frac{1}{3600}=\frac{200}{3600}\approx\boxed{0.056\ \text{km}\approx56\ \text{m}}.\]

10:
Lagrange with $g=x^4y^2z=1$ ($x,y,z>0$): $2x=\lambda\cdot4x^3y^2z$, $2y=\lambda\cdot2x^4yz$, $2z=\lambda x^4y^2$. Multiply by $x$, $y$, $z$ and use $g=1$: $x^2=2\lambda$, $y^2=\lambda$, $z^2=\frac\lambda2$. Then $x^4y^2z=4\lambda^2\cdot\lambda\cdot\sqrt{\lambda/2}=1\Rightarrow\lambda=2^{-3/7}$:
\[\boxed{x\approx1.219,\quad y\approx0.862,\quad z\approx0.610}\qquad(M_{\min}=\tfrac72\lambda\approx2.600).\]
